hypotheses.justification: The statement elaborates without it, and it appears to be true in general; I did not prove the general case in Lean. The only place the proof uses it is `epi_whiskerRight_of_epi p₁` for the covering hypothesis `hv`. Without it, factor p₁ = e ≫ m with e epi and m mono (image factorisation in the abelian category). In a rigid category `m ▷ W₂` is mono, since tensoring is exact, i.e. `tensorRight` preserves limits. Since p₁ ⊗ₘ p₂ = (e ▷ Z₂) ≫ (I ◁ p₂) ≫ (m ▷ W₂), the kernel of p₁ ⊗ₘ p₂ equals the kernel of (e ▷ Z₂) ≫ (I ◁ p₂). The existing argument applied to the epi e (with I in place of W₁) bounds this by ker(e ▷ Z₂) ⊔ im(Z₁ ◁ ker ι p₂), and `kernelSubobject_whiskerRight_le` bounds ker(e ▷ Z₂) by im(kernel.ι e ▷ Z₂). Since m is mono, kernel.ι e and kernel.ι p₁ differ by an isomorphism, so the images of their whiskerings agree. Degenerate check: if p₁ = 0 then kernel.ι p₁ is an isomorphism, so the right side is ⊤ and the claim holds.
